description: The successful subscription example has no success field and matches both the success object and the validation-error object, whose success=false field is optional. OpenAPI oneOf therefore rejects it. The harness falls back to the validation-error example, which the node correctly reports as error.

The documented success response returns sorts as arrays of timestamp arrays; its schema requires object items. The node preserves that response and accepts returned cursor arrays. The harness instead selects the spec-valid validation-error example.

The FOUND and NOT_FOUND response oneOf branches have identical string types without status discriminators, so the documented NOT_FOUND example matches both. The node accepts the published response; the harness falls back to the validation-error example.

The published success response omits results.saasServices required by the schema, and returns sorts as timestamp/id arrays rather than the declared object items. The node preserves the published response; the harness falls back to the validation-error example.

The published NOT_FOUND response has results (plural), whereas both success schemas require result (singular). The node preserves either response; the harness falls back to the validation-error example.
The published NOT_FOUND response has result:null, but both success schemas require an object. The node preserves null; the harness falls back to the validation-error example.

The two request oneOf branches have the same structural constraints and no const/enum on type; every documented request matches both. The published response also has foundedYear as a string (schema: number), employeeGrowth entries without required growth, no required company id, and result:null for NOT_FOUND (schema: object). The node sends the exact published request and preserves the exact published response.
